title: Jack Ging: OU Halfback Who Became a Hollywood Actor
question: Which former Oklahoma football player became an actor on The A-Team and Mannix?
answer: Jack Ging, a halfback at Oklahoma from 1951 to 1953, became a longtime television and film actor. He played General Bull Fulbright on The A-Team and Lt. Dan Ives on Mannix.
summary: Alva native Jack Ging played halfback at OU from 1951 to 1953, then built a Hollywood career with Mannix, The A-Team and several Clint Eastwood films.
body: Not every Sooner who left Norman headed for the NFL. Jack Ging, born in Alva, Oklahoma, in 1931, headed for Hollywood.

Ging served four years in the U.S. Marine Corps before college. At Oklahoma, SoonerStats lists him on the roster for three seasons, 1951 through 1953, wearing No. 11 and listed at 5-foot-10 and 152 pounds. He scored five touchdowns as a Sooner, and he was part of the team in the 1954 Orange Bowl. After graduating he played one season in the Canadian Football League with the Edmonton Eskimos.

Acting came next. Ging's screen career ran from the late 1950s into the 1990s and included more than 50 film and television roles. He joined the final season of the western Tales of Wells Fargo as Beau McCloud, played Dr. Paul Graham on The Eleventh Hour, and appeared regularly as Lt. Dan Ives on the detective series Mannix.

He also worked with Clint Eastwood, with parts in Hang 'Em High, Play Misty for Me and High Plains Drifter. Many viewers in the 1980s knew him best as General Harlan Bull Fulbright, the general who crossed paths with the title team on NBC's The A-Team. He also played Lt. Ted Quinlan on Riptide.
Ging died on September 9, 2022, at his home in La Quinta, California, at the age of 90.
